slides.texte_overlay:
How To Become Socially
Confident Fast
Talk to one new person every day. The cashier, a colleague, a neighbour. Small daily reps make talking to people feel normal instead of terrifying.
Go to events alone sometimes. Without a friend to hide behind, you're forced to talk to new people, and you discover you're much better at it than you think.
Prepare your answer to common questions. "What do you do?", "Where are you from?" A relaxed, interesting answer ready in advance takes the panic out of small talk.
Say yes to invitations, even when you're tired. Every evening out is practice. Confidence grows from showing up, not from waiting until you feel ready.
Before: nothing to talk about, so I avoided people. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a head full of topics that makes talking easy.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: nothing to talk about, so I avoided people. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now my head is full of topics to share.

slides.texte_overlay: Notice when it goes well. After a good chat, take a second to register it. Remembering your wins is how your brain learns that social moments are safe.
Forgive yourself for awkward moments. Everyone has them. The confident people you admire just stopped replaying them at night. Let them go and try again tomorrow.
